question: In which year did the Government of India start setting up Regional Rural Banks?
solution:
The correct answer is In __**1975**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• RRBs were created under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976 (Not Banking Regulation Act) to serve the credit need of rural areas which were largely unbanked at that time.
 
• The ownership of RRBs as per the Act is Central government (50%), State government (15%), and Sponsor bank (35%). RBI has no ownership of RRBs.
 
• Post-1991 reforms have seen RRBs being allowed to expand its affairs in the non-priority sector to offset its losses.
 
• Each RRB must have a sponsor bank which exercises 355 ownership rights. It helps RRB provide direction and expertise
